topic_name: Will, regulation of behavior and theories of emotion

266.question: The conscious regulation of behavior in overcoming internal and external obstacles is called...

options.B: A set (attitude)
options.C: Self-awareness
options.E: Will

267.question: A person refrains from an impulsive response that is incompatible with his or her convictions. Which function of will is realized?

options.B: Inhibitory
options.C: Motivating
options.E: Evaluative

268.question: Initiating an action on the basis of a current internal impulse expresses the... function of will.

options.B: Evaluative
options.C: Inhibitory
options.E: Orienting

options.A: It is reduced solely to an increase in activity
options.B: It is completely independent of convictions
options.C: It excludes the inhibition of significant drives
options.D: It makes it possible to strengthen some motives and restrain others
options.E: It unites the motivating and inhibitory functions

270.question: What shortcoming do spoiling and excessive suppression of a child have in common that hinders the development of will?

options.A: A lack of practice in making decisions and exerting effort independently
options.B: Heightened difference sensitivity
options.C: An excess of independent responsibility
options.E: Explaining the meaning of demands too often

271.question: Which method of upbringing directly supports the development of will?

options.B: Doing the difficult part for the child in advance
options.C: Unfailingly deciding any questions for the child
options.E: Helping the child find a solution and carry it out independently

272.question: Comparing the expected and the achieved result of a volitional action is connected primarily with the participation of...

options.A: The parietal lobes of the brain
options.B: The temporal lobes of the brain
options.C: The occipital lobes of the brain
options.E: The frontal lobes of the brain

273.question: Which combination consists specifically of volitional qualities?

options.B: Resolve, persistence, self-control
options.C: Constancy, objectivity, wholeness
options.E: Extraversion, neuroticism, endomorphy

274.question: Statements that distinguish the intellectualist and the peripheral theories of emotion:

options.A: Both approaches explained emotions only by reinforcement
options.B: Herbart linked feelings with the relations among mental representations
options.C: Wundt considered emotion only a reaction of a peripheral organ
options.D: James and Lange assigned the primary role to bodily changes
options.E: James completely denied bodily feedback

275.question: The author of The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals, who developed an evolutionary explanation of emotions, was...

options.B: L. Festinger
options.C: P. V. Simonov
options.E: W. James

276.question: What is the sequence in which an emotion arises in the James-Lange theory?

options.A: Stimulus, simultaneous experience and bodily reaction
options.B: Stimulus, comparison of expectations, elimination of dissonance
options.C: Stimulus, appraisal of a need, emergence of an intention
options.E: Stimulus, bodily changes, experience of them

277.question: Which objection did W. Cannon raise against the peripheral theory of emotion?

options.A: Different emotions always have a unique visceral pattern
options.B: Experience is possible only after a conscious decision
options.C: Similar bodily changes accompany different emotions
options.D: Emotional expression is unrelated to the organism
options.E: Organic changes are always completely absent

278.question: The occurrence of emotional experience and bodily changes almost simultaneously corresponds to the approach of...

options.B: Cannon and Bard
options.C: Schachter's cognitive-physiological approach
options.E: Lindsley and Hebb

279.question: Indicate the correct correspondences between theories of emotion.

options.A: Darwin: the adaptive origin of expression
options.B: Festinger: the balance of body fluids
options.C: Lindsley and Hebb: the level of neural activation
options.D: Schachter: complete exclusion of the appraisal of the situation
options.E: James and Lange: the experience of bodily changes

280.question: Emotional states are linked with the reticular formation and the level of activity of the nervous system by the...

options.B: Humoral theory of Hippocrates
options.C: Associative theory of Ebbinghaus
options.E: Activation theory of Lindsley and Hebb

281.question: Which relationship between arousal and the effectiveness of activity did D. O. Hebb describe?

options.A: Any increase in arousal completely blocks activity
options.B: The stronger the arousal, the better the result, without limit
options.C: The level of arousal is unrelated to task performance
options.D: Excessively weak and excessively strong arousal can reduce effectiveness
options.E: Effectiveness is always at its maximum when there is no arousal at all

282.question: Discomfort caused by psychologically contradictory information about an object is explained by the concept of...

options.B: Perceptual isomorphism
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.E: Motor inertia

283.question: Taking bodily arousal into account together with a subjective appraisal of the situation is characteristic of the theory of emotion of...

options.B: S. Schachter
options.C: E. Kretschmer
options.E: D. Broadbent

284.question: Correct statements about cognitive theories of emotion:

options.B: Need and available information are taken into account in Simonov's theory
options.C: Context is excluded from Schachter's model
options.D: A subjective appraisal can change the experience
options.E: Simonov explains emotion only by body build

285.question: In P. V. Simonov's information theory, the essential link is between emotion and...

options.A: The proportion of the endomorphic and mesomorphic components
options.B: Exclusively the number of previously repeated reactions
options.C: Only the absolute strength of a physical stimulus
options.D: A current need and the ratio of necessary to available information
options.E: A fixed innate scheme of emotional expression
